title: Transcriptional condensates encode a "golden mean" to optimize enhancer-promoter communication across genomic distances.
authors: Zhu, Tao; Li, Chunhe; Chu, Xiakun
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
one_liner_zh: 该文用聚合物染色质模拟研究转录因子凝聚体对增强子-启动子长距离通讯的调控机制，虽非直接TF-DNA结合建模，但聚焦TF介导的染色质互作动态，方法可迁移至TF-DNA互作机制研究。
abstract: Enhancers regulate gene expression by physically contacting their target promoters, yet these contacts often span large genomic distances. Phase-separated condensates (droplet-like clusters) of transcription factors (TFs) are thought to facilitate such long-range enhancer-promoter (E-P) communication, but the quantitative principles underlying this mechanism remain unclear. Here, we use polymer-based chromatin simulations to systematically vary the strength of TF clustering and the E-P genomic distance, examining their combined effects on E-P contact formation. We find that E-P contact frequency shows a nonmonotonic dependence on the degree of TF clustering: Contact frequency peaks at an intermediate TF abundance and TF-TF affinity, leading to a "golden mean" optimum. Two distinct regimes emerge: Under weak TF-TF attraction, contact probability increases with condensate size, whereas strong TF attraction produces a peaked response that declines at high condensation levels. These results indicate that TF condensate acts as a tunable "rheostat," buffering E-P interactions against increasing genomic distances. However, excessive TF clustering leads to molecular crowding and competition that ultimately impair E-P communication. Our study, consistent with recent experiments, establishes a mechanistic framework at the molecular level, where balanced TF condensation enables robust long-range E-P communication, reconciling the stochastic nature of chromatin dynamics with the fidelity of gene regulation.
abstract_zh: 增强子通过物理接触其靶标启动子来调控基因表达，然而这些接触往往跨越较大的基因组距离。转录因子（TFs）的相分离凝聚体（液滴状簇）被认为有助于这种长距离增强子-启动子（E-P）通讯，但这一机制背后的定量原理仍不清楚。在此，我们使用基于聚合物的染色质模拟，系统性地改变TF聚集强度及E-P基因组距离，考察它们对E-P接触形成的联合效应。我们发现，E-P接触频率对TF聚集程度呈非单调依赖：接触频率在中等TF丰度和TF-TF亲和力时达到峰值，形成“黄金中庸”最优状态。出现两种截然不同的机制区间：在弱TF-TF吸引力下，接触概率随凝聚体大小增加而增加，而强TF吸引力则产生峰值响应，在高凝聚水平下下降。这些结果表明，TF凝聚体充当可调“变阻器”，缓冲E-P相互作用以应对增加的基因组距离。然而，过度的TF聚集导致分子拥挤和竞争，最终损害E-P通讯。我们的研究，与近期实验一致，在分子层面建立了一个机制框架，其中平衡的TF凝聚使稳健的长距离E-P通讯成为可能，调和了染色质动力学的随机性与基因调控的保真度。
